subject: ACME POC — eval methodology alignment and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC — post-call recap + proposed evaluation approach

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the formal SOW/POC kickoff:

Summary of call:
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for ACME’s customer support summarization use case (10k monthly conversations).
- Success metrics discussed: extractive summary accuracy, downstream CSAT delta, average latency under 280ms p95, and per-1000-token cost target.
- Constraints: must not send PHI to third-party hosted endpoints; prefer VPC/private deployment for evaluation or a privacy-preserving shadowing approach.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Week 0: Finalize success criteria & eval plan (owners: ACME product + Redwood AE).
2) Weeks 1–2: Offline evals — we run curated test set (anonymized) against candidate models and report graded rubric.
3) Weeks 3–4: Online shadowing (optional, gated) — send non-responding traffic in mirrored mode to Redwood Dedicated in ACME VPC; monitor latency, reliability, and quality.
4) Week 5: Joint review and recommendation.

Open items / asks for ACME:
- Please confirm the success criteria in the attached spreadsheet (ACME_POC_success_criteria.xlsx).
- Indicate whether you prefer us to start with offline evals only or run parallel light-weight shadowing in Week 3. Note: shadowing requires short advance coordination with security/networking for VPC peering.
- Assign an internal owner for data prep and for approval of the anonymized test set.

Evaluation methodology options (short):
- Offline evals: Redwood runs anonymized test sets in our secure environment; we compute precision/recall, ROUGE scores where applicable, latency histograms, and a graded rubric. Fast, low-risk.
- Online shadow: Mirror production requests (no responses returned to customers) to measure end-to-end latency and real-world failure modes. Higher fidelity but needs networking & privacy sign-off.

I attached a first-draft evaluation plan (evaluation_plan_v1.docx) and a starter success-criteria workbook. I’m looping Dylan and Rachel from our delivery/QA teams to comment on feasibility and rubric.

Next steps I suggest:
- ACME reviews and confirms the success criteria by Thu, Aug 12.
- If you want shadowing, let us know by Mon, Aug 16 so we can kick off networking approvals.

Thanks — Marissa

Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — post-call recap + proposed evaluation approach

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with our internal thinking. A few clarifications and minor edits to the success criteria:

- We prefer a combined quality metric: accuracy (ROUGE-L / semantic match) >= 0.72 on the anonymized corpus AND a manual rubriked score average >= 3.5/5 on a 200-sample blind review.
- CSAT uplift is a stretch goal — we'll track it but won't gate the POC on it.
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms is acceptable for the first pass.

About offline vs shadowing: we want to do both if possible. Start with offline evals for baseline results; if offline results are promising, proceed to light shadowing for 7–10 business days to validate latency and failure modes. We'll need to loop in our infra/security to approve VPC peering. Priya will coordinate.

Owners:
- Data/test set owner: Priya Shah (she will share anonymized samples)
- Business owner: Liam O'Connor

We can confirm the success criteria by Thu Aug 12. Please have Dylan send a proposed rubric so Priya and I can review.

Thanks,
Liam

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — post-call recap + proposed evaluation approach

Thanks — good plan. A few notes from delivery/QA perspective and a proposed grading rubric (attached as eval_rubric.csv):

1) Recommended phased approach (minimal risk):
   - Phase A (Days 0–10): Offline evals only. Redwood will run the anonymized test set against three candidate model configurations (fp16, int8-quant, and our tuned small-L2). We'll produce a comparison table (ROUGE, semantic similarity, latency distribution).
   - Phase B (Days 11–20): Conditional shadowing if Phase A meets the quality thresholds (ROUGE-L >= 0.72 and manual avg >= 3.5). Shadowing window: 7 business days with throttling to 5% of production QPS initially.

2) Grading rubric (high-level):
   - Quality (50%): ROUGE / semantic similarity aggregated; manual blind review scores (0–5) weighted.
   - Reliability (20%): error rate, timeouts per 10k requests.
   - Latency (15%): p50/p95/p99; p95 must be <= 300ms to pass.
   - Cost (10%): projected per-1k-token run cost compared to target.
   - Privacy/Compliance (5%): no data exfiltration, confirm VPC/isolation requirements.

3) Deliverables and owners:
   - Evaluation runner and baseline report: Redwood (Dylan) — due Aug 24.
   - Shadowing setup & network coordination: ACME infra (Priya) + Redwood infra (Rachel) — target Aug 18 for network readiness.
   - Joint review meeting: Aug 25 — 30-minute review (Marissa to own scheduling).

4) Quick technical caveats:
   - For shadowing we will not persist logs to any external S3 buckets without explicit sign-off. We can stream anonymized telemetry to your GCS in your VPC for analysis.
   - If ACME requires on-prem / air-gapped eval, that adds lead time; please flag now.

Next steps (short):
- Marissa: Confirm schedule & meeting invite.
- Priya: Share anonymized test set by Fri Aug 13 (preferred).
- ACME infra + Redwood infra: confirm network checklist by Aug 18.

Dylan

Agreed approach:
- Phase A (Days 0–10): Offline evals only (Redwood runs tests on anonymized set).
- Phase B (Days 11–20): Conditional shadowing (7 business days, up to 5% QPS) if Phase A meets thresholds.

Finalized success thresholds: ROUGE-L >= 0.72 AND manual blind review average >= 3.5/5. Latency p95 <= 300ms.
